Table spreads vs base: C 3->380, D 6->760, A 8->990, F 12->1490, B 16->2010, E 20->2480, monotonic over all six. 10 lies between A (8, 990) and F (12, 1490), so 990-1490 m. items.recognised_real_data: The table follows the textbook lifting-condensation-level rule, cloud base ~ 125 m x (T - Td): 8->1000 (990), 16->2000 (2010), 3->375 (380), 6->750 (760), 20->2500 (2480), 12->1500 (1490), all within 20 m. A student who knows the rule computes 10 x 125 = 1250 m without the table. Passage-level: the shared table is this formula.

items.cold_note: Temperature and UV covary with elevation in the field, so only a factorial that decouples them (cold/warm x high/low UV, one seed source) distinguishes S1 (hair tracks UV) from S2 (hair tracks temperature). A repeats the confounded elevation gradient; D is one elevation and one aspect with no comparison; B tests whether hairs aid growth, which both explanations predict.

free_elimination.how: D measures one condition (one elevation, one aspect) and computes an average: with no comparison it cannot distinguish any two explanations.

items.note: Key correct: S1 ties hair density to UV, S2 to temperature; both covary with elevation, so only a design decoupling them distinguishes.
